What is the difference between JasperReports and Jaspersoft Studio?

JasperReports is the Java library you embed in the application to compile templates, fill them with data and export them. Jaspersoft Studio is the Eclipse-based designer used to build and preview .jrxml templates visually. A separate product, JasperReports Server, adds a web repository and scheduling, but a Spring Boot app only needs the library.
What is the difference between .jrxml and .jasper?

.jrxml is the XML source template, editable and kept in version control. .jasper is the compiled binary JasperReport produced by JasperCompileManager, with expressions already compiled. Loading a .jasper avoids the compile cost at runtime, but it must match the library version, so many teams compile from .jrxml at build time or startup.
Explain the compile → fill → export lifecycle.

Compile turns the jrxml into a JasperReport. Fill combines the report with parameters and a data source or JDBC connection to produce a JasperPrint (the paginated pages in memory). Export renders that JasperPrint to PDF, XLSX, HTML and so on. One JasperPrint can be exported to several formats without filling again.
Name the report bands and when each prints.

Title (once at the start), Page Header (every page), Column Header (above the details on each page), Detail (once per record), Column Footer, Page Footer (every page; Last Page Footer on the final page), Summary (once at the end), plus Group Header/Footer around each group, Background, and No Data. 💡 Put totals in the Summary or group footers and page numbers in the Page Footer.
Fields vs parameters vs variables?

Fields ($F{}) are values from the current record of the data source. Parameters ($P{}) are inputs passed in at fill time, such as filters, titles, images or subreports. Variables ($V{}) are computed during the fill, like sums, counts and averages, with a reset scope of Report, Page or Group, plus built-ins such as PAGE_NUMBER and REPORT_COUNT.
What is the difference between $P{} and $P!{} in a report query?

$P{x} becomes a bind parameter in a prepared statement, which is safe from SQL injection. $P!{x} pastes the text into the SQL before execution, which is useful for a dynamic ORDER BY column or an optional WHERE clause. Because it is not bound, only pass whitelisted values, never raw user input.
JDBC connection vs JRBeanCollectionDataSource — which do you choose?

With a JDBC connection the SQL lives in the report. It is quick for large tabular reports and lets the database do the work, but the query is hidden from application code and tests. With JRBeanCollectionDataSource, your service layer loads DTOs (reusing repositories, security filters and business logic) and the report is only a view. The downside is that the whole collection sits in memory. Many teams use beans for documents (invoices, prescriptions) and JDBC or a streaming custom data source for big listings.
How do subreports work and what are their pitfalls?

A subreport element embeds another compiled report. You pass it via a parameter or expression and give it either the master's connection plus linking parameters or a nested data source, e.g. new JRBeanCollectionDataSource($F{lines}). Results can go back through return values. The main pitfall is performance: a subreport in the Detail band runs per row, which causes N+1 queries. Paths to subreport files also break when you move from Studio to the server, so pass compiled objects as parameters.
How do you show "Page X of Y"?

Use two text fields. The first is "Page " + $V{PAGE_NUMBER} with evaluation time Now. The second is " of " + $V{PAGE_NUMBER} with evaluation time Report, so it is filled in after all pages exist and shows the total. Put both fields in the Page Footer. Jaspersoft Studio's palette also has ready-made "Page X of Y" elements that set this up for you.
How do you generate and return a PDF from a Spring Boot endpoint?

Load or cache the compiled report, build the parameter map and data source, call JasperFillManager.fillReport, then JasperExportManager.exportReportToPdf. Return the bytes with Content-Type: application/pdf and a Content-Disposition of inline or attachment. Check authorization before loading the data. For big files, stream to the response output stream with JRPdfExporter and SimpleOutputStreamExporterOutput.
How do you export to Excel properly?

Use JRXlsxExporter with SimpleXlsxReportConfiguration: detectCellType for real numbers and dates, removeEmptySpaceBetweenRows, and onePagePerSheet(false). Fill with IS_IGNORE_PAGINATION=true so headers do not repeat every page. Lay out elements on a strict grid with no overlaps. Otherwise Excel output ends up with merged or empty cells. 💡 For pure data dumps, a CSV export or Apache POI is often simpler than a designed report.
How do you add a chart to a report?

Drop a chart element (bar, pie, line, time series) into the Summary or a group footer and configure its dataset: series, category and value expressions over fields. The dataset is filled as records are iterated, and the chart is rendered (via JFreeChart) when the band prints. If the chart needs different data than the main report, use a sub-dataset with its own query or data source.
A large report causes OutOfMemoryError. What do you do?

Pass a virtualizer (JRSwapFileVirtualizer/JRFileVirtualizer) in REPORT_VIRTUALIZER so filled pages are written to disk. Use a JDBC or streaming data source instead of loading a huge bean list. Aggregate in SQL, remove per-row subreports, and stream the export instead of building a byte[]. Then run it as an async job with limited concurrency and, if needed, more heap.
Fonts look wrong or characters are missing in the PDF. Why?

The PDF exporter only uses fonts it can find and embed. Server JVMs (especially Docker images) often lack the font that was used in Studio, or the font has no glyphs for the language. Fix it by packaging a font extension JAR (export it from Studio), referencing that font family in the template, and enabling PDF embedding. That gives identical output on every machine and correct Unicode rendering.
How do you improve JasperReports performance in general?

Compile once (build-time .jasper or a cache), optimize and index the SQL, aggregate in the database, avoid subreports inside the Detail band, use virtualizers for huge outputs, keep images small, reuse one JasperPrint for several formats, and generate heavy reports asynchronously with a bounded thread pool so they do not starve request threads.
Why does the same group header appear several times in my report?

Groups break whenever the group expression value changes from one record to the next; they don't sort the data. If the query isn't ordered by the group field, the same department appears in several separate runs. Add ORDER BY department (and nested group fields in order) or define sort fields in the dataset.
How do you show subtotals per group and a grand total?

Create a variable with calculation="Sum", resetType="Group" and resetGroup="dept" and place it in the group footer; create another with resetType="Report" for the Summary band. A variable shown in a group header needs evaluationTime="Group" to display the final value rather than the current running value.
What is a Print When Expression?

A Boolean expression on an element or band that controls whether it is printed, e.g. show a "DISCOUNT" label only when $F{discount} != null, or print a band only on the first page with $V{PAGE_NUMBER} == 1. Combine it with "Remove line when blank" to avoid empty gaps.
How do you highlight overdue rows in red?

Define a style with a conditional style whose condition is $F{dueDate}.before(new java.util.Date()) (or a Boolean field computed in the service) and set the forecolor or backcolor; apply the style to the detail text fields or a background rectangle. Alternating row colours use $V{REPORT_COUNT} % 2 == 0.
When would you use a crosstab instead of a table?

When both rows and columns come from data, i.e. a pivot such as revenue by product (rows) and month (columns), with totals in both directions. A table component has fixed columns defined at design time with rows from a dataset. Crosstabs can grow wide, so consider landscape pages or Excel export.
How do you produce the same report in several languages?

Put labels in resource bundles (labels_en.properties, labels_ta.properties), reference them with $R{key} or str("key"), and pass REPORT_LOCALE when filling. Use locale-aware patterns for dates and numbers, and embed fonts that contain the required glyphs so the PDF renders correctly.
How do you add a logo that works when the app runs from a JAR?

Don't use an absolute file path. Load it from the classpath and pass it as a parameter of type java.io.InputStream or java.awt.Image, then use $P{LOGO} as the image expression. Keep it cached so it isn't re-read for every page.
Why does my Excel export have repeated headers and empty rows?

The layout is page-oriented: page headers and footers repeat for every page and absolute positioning creates spacer rows and merged cells. For data exports, fill with IS_IGNORE_PAGINATION set to true (one long page), use XLSX export settings such as removing empty space between rows, detecting cell types and one-page-per-sheet off, and align elements to a clean column grid. Often a dedicated data-only report or a direct Apache POI/CSV export is better.
Should you compile the .jrxml on every request?

No. Compilation is slow (it generates and compiles expression classes). Compile at build time (the Maven plugin produces .jasper) or compile once at startup and cache the JasperReport object, which is thread-safe to reuse. Each request then only fills and exports.
What are scriptlets, and should you use them?

Scriptlets are Java classes extending JRDefaultScriptlet or JRAbstractScriptlet with callbacks during report filling (before/after report, page, group, detail), able to read and set variables. They help with complex running calculations, but they hide logic inside the report. In modern apps, compute values in the service layer and pass ready data through a bean data source.
Subreport vs table component vs list component?

| Subreport | Table component | List component
Lives in | A separate .jrxml, compiled on its own | The main .jrxml, using a sub-dataset | The main .jrxml, using a sub-dataset
Layout | Anything: its own bands and groups | Rows and columns with headers and footers | A free-form cell repeated per row
Data | Own query or data source per instance | Dataset run with its own query or data source | Dataset run
Cost inside a detail band | Filled once per master row, can be slow | Also runs per master row | Also runs per master row
Best for | Complex nested sections, reused pieces | Simple tabular detail | Cards or label-value blocks
Rule of thumb: reach for a table for plain tabular detail and keep subreports for layouts a table cannot express. For big master-detail reports, a single joined query with groups is usually faster than either.
Text field evaluation time: Now vs Report vs Page vs Group vs Auto?

evaluationTime | Value is calculated | Typical use
Now (default) | When the band is filled | Normal fields
Page | At the end of the current page | Page totals shown in the page header
Group | When the named group ends | Group total shown in the group header
Report | At the end of the whole report | "of Y" in "Page X of Y", grand total on page 1
Auto | Each variable at its own reset time | Mixing values like "3 of 120 rows" in one field
Interview tip: "Page X of Y" uses two text fields over $V{PAGE_NUMBER}: one with Now for X and one with Report for Y.
PDF vs XLSX vs CSV vs HTML export: what changes?

| PDF | XLSX | CSV | HTML
Layout fidelity | Pixel-perfect | Fit to a cell grid | None, data only | Close, but browser-dependent
Pagination | Real pages | Often unwanted; turn page breaks off | None | Optional
Fonts | Must be embedded via font extensions | Uses Excel fonts | Not relevant | Browser fonts
User wants to | Print, sign, archive | Sort, filter, sum | Import into another system | View in the app
Design tip | Free layout | Align fields to columns, no overlaps | One field per column | Avoid absolute positioning tricks
Rule of thumb: one JasperPrint can go to every format, but a design tuned for PDF rarely looks good in Excel. If both matter, keep a separate grid-friendly design for spreadsheet output.
